`final class DrawResource`<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.lib.draw.resource` · **Module:** `core` · **Source:** [DrawResource.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/core/src/main/java/dev/joid/lib/draw/resource/DrawResource.java)

Draws resources and GPU textures, tinted by the current color of the render state.

## Description

Reach it through `DrawUtils.RESOURCE`.
Positions and sizes are in design pixels, in the coordinates you draw in.
The image is multiplied by the current color of the render state: bind a [`Color`](/reference/drawing/color/) around the call to tint it or fade it.

A drawn resource asks its decoder for the size it covers in screen pixels, so a vector image stays sharp, and turns on mipmaps by itself when it is drawn smaller than its texture with linear filtering.
A resource that is still loading draws nothing; a failed resource draws a checkerboard in dev mode and nothing otherwise.

## Method details

<a id="DrawResource-method-drawResource"></a>

### drawResource

`void drawResource(double x, double y, Resource resource)` 

Draws the resource at `x`, `y` at its own size, [`Resource.getWidth`](/reference/resources/resource/#Resource-method-getWidth) × [`Resource.getHeight`](/reference/resources/resource/#Resource-method-getHeight).

`void drawResource(double x, double y, double width, double height, Resource resource)` 

Draws the resource stretched to `width` × `height`.

`void drawResource(double x, double y, double width, double height, double u, double v, double regionWidth, double regionHeight, Resource resource)` 

Draws a region of the image stretched to `width` × `height`: the region starts at `u`, `v` and spans `regionWidth` × `regionHeight`, in pixels of the source image.
When the resource has its own region (`textureCoords`), `u` and `v` count from the corner of that region.

<a id="DrawResource-method-drawTexture"></a>

### drawTexture

`void drawTexture(double x, double y, double width, double height, ITexture texture, double u0, double v0, double u1, double v1, TextureFilter filter, BlendState blend)` 

Draws a raw GPU texture, such as the color texture of a [`FrameBuffer`](/reference/drawing/framebuffer/), stretched to `width` × `height`, with the filter and the blending you pass.
`u0`, `v0` and `u1`, `v1` are the texture coordinates of the top-left and bottom-right corners, on 1; swap `v0` and `v1` to flip the image.
